commits.subject: Harden TTS: timeout Groq call, trim replies, surface raw errors
commits.body:
- Add an 8s AbortController timeout around the Groq TTS request so a
  slow render fails with our own error instead of letting Netlify's
  ~10s function limit kill it silently (which was likely producing the
  empty "No audio returned" with no detail — a platform-level timeout
  response isn't shaped like our JSON error body)
- Cap voice replies at 600 chars, cut at a sentence boundary — also
  just better UX than reading a full essay aloud in a call
- Frontend now reads the raw response body first and shows the actual
  HTTP status + error text if it ever fails again, instead of masking
  everything as "No audio returned"

commits.subject: Fix critical TDZ crash that silently broke most of the app; CC captions
commits.body:
The real bug behind everything reported: tryResumeSession() was called
near the top of the script (to avoid a startup-screen flash), but it
transitively calls getMemory(), which reads `settings` — a variable
declared much further down in the same script. Accessing a let/const
before its declaration line executes throws a ReferenceError (temporal
dead zone), and an uncaught error during synchronous top-level script
execution halts everything after it. Every declaration, event listener,
and init call below that point in the file never ran: Settings clicks
did nothing, the send button never got its 'input' listener (so it
never morphed), Live Voice's call state was never initialized, wake
word never armed, tips never started rotating — one crash, cascading
into what looked like a dozen unrelated bugs.

Fix: moved tryResumeSession()/tryResumeOwnerSession() to the true end
of the script, after every declaration has run.

Added scripts/check-init.js (npm run check:init) — actually executes
the inline script's init code against a stub DOM in real Node/V8,
rather than just grepping for names, so this exact class of runtime
error gets caught before it ships next time.

Also:
- Live Voice call screen now shows the same wallpaper background as
  the rest of the app instead of a heavily blurred view of the chat
  transcript behind it
- Added a CC button (on by default) that shows Knowura's spoken
  replies as on-screen captions while it talks

commits.subject: Add ChatGPT-style sidebar with per-chat guest storage, drop Clear Memory for Delete All Chats
commits.body:
Guest chats now live in knowura_guest_chats (multi-chat, searchable, rename/delete
per chat), migrated automatically from the old single-thread knowura_chat. Clear
Memory is replaced by Delete All Chats since memory clearing wasn't pulling its
weight once chats have their own lifecycle.

commits.subject: Add server-verified Google sign-in and cloud chat storage functions
commits.body:
Phase 2: onSignIn() now posts the Google credential to a new
google-signin-verify.js function, which checks it against Google's
tokeninfo endpoint (aud/exp) instead of trusting a client-decoded JWT, and
issues a signed session token (_userToken.js, same HMAC pattern as owner
mode) keyed to the verified sub. Signed-in users still ride the local/guest
chat store for now — cloud sync isn't wired up yet (phase 4) — but the
session itself is real. logOut() clears the new session fields too.

Phase 3: chat-load.js / chat-save.js store a per-user cloud document
(chats + memory) in Netlify Blobs, keyed by the verified sub from the
session token — never a client-supplied id. chat-save.js additionally
cross-checks the document's own profile.sub against the token before
writing, so a valid session can never overwrite another account's blob.

Documents the two new env vars (GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID, KNOWURA_USER_TOKEN_SECRET)
and functions in the README.

commits.subject: Wire signed-in users onto cloud chat sync; finish sidebar polish
commits.body:
Phase 4: signed-in (Google) sessions now actually use chat-load.js/
chat-save.js instead of just carrying a verified-but-unused token. On
sign-in/resume, loadCloudChats() pulls the account's chat+memory doc; if
none exists yet (new account) it offers to import this device's local
guest chats non-destructively, then seeds the cloud doc. Every chat/memory
mutation for a cloud user (saveChatStore, extractFacts, maybeSummarize)
now schedules a debounced (1.5s) full-document save via persistCloudStore,
flushed immediately on tab-hide so nothing is lost to the debounce window.
Guest mode is untouched — still pure localStorage, gated by isCloudUser().

logOut() now clears all in-memory chat/profile/memory state (chatStore,
userProfile, cloudMemory, chat-box DOM) so a second sign-in never
flashes the previous account's chats — closes a gap the old logOut() had.

Phase 5: sidebar collapse state already persisted via settings, mobile
slide-in overlay and rename/delete already in place from phase 1 — verified
all still wired correctly after the auth/data-flow changes.

commits.subject: Exclude GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID from Netlify secrets scanning
commits.body:
It's not a secret — Google OAuth client IDs are meant to be public and
are intentionally hardcoded in public/index.html (data-client_id) for
Google Identity Services. Netlify's build-output scanner flagged it as a
leaked secret since its value matches an env var, failing the build.

commits.subject: Fix music panel overflowing the viewport in the sidebar footer; correct Qwen model id
commits.body:
The music panel used to drop down from a header button; now anchored in the
sidebar footer, a fixed left:0/300px-wide panel ran off the right edge of
both the sidebar and the viewport on narrow screens. Scoped the panel to
open upward and right-align within the sidebar footer instead, capped to
the viewport width, using an ancestor-scoped selector (.sidebar-footer
.music-panel) so it reliably beats the plain .music-panel rule regardless
of source order or the mobile media query.

Also corrected the Qwen model id to qwen/qwen3.6-27b (was qwen/qwen3-32b).

commits.subject: Fix voice mode breaking on mobile from wake-word listener fighting the call's mic
commits.body:
On mobile, the default "Voice Mode Only" wake word setting started a
Web Speech API SpeechRecognition session (Google's own mic-listening
stream, with its native listening indicator) at the same time the call's
own getUserMedia/VAD stream was active. Two concurrent mic consumers broke
the call on mobile Chrome. applyWakeWordSetting() now skips starting the
wake listener on mobile while a call is open — desktop is unaffected.

Also moved the is-mobile/is-touch detection consts to the top of the
script instead of near the bottom, since the wake-word code (much earlier
in the file) now needs to read them — same TDZ pattern this file already
got bitten by once this session.

commits.subject: Swap DotGothic16 for Geist Pixel across every font-family declaration
Fix Qwen raw <think> blocks leaking into the visible reply
commits.body:
Groq's OSS models return chain-of-thought separately (message.reasoning),
which already had a collapsible "Thought Process" section — but Qwen3.6
wraps its thinking inline as a leading <think>...</think> block directly
inside message.content instead. That raw block was rendering verbatim as
the actual chat reply (what looked like garbled internal monologue full
of fabricated facts was literally the model's unstripped thinking text).
Now strips that leading block out of the reply and routes it into the same
Thought Process dropdown OSS reasoning already uses.

commits.subject: Add a way to reset stored facts/summary independent of chat history
commits.body:
Deleting Clear Memory earlier removed the only way to recover from bad
data getting stuck in facts/summary (e.g. the <think>-leak bug feeding a
fabricated persona into fact-extraction) — Delete All Chats never touched
facts/summary, so a poisoned fact had no fix. Adds "Forget Remembered
Facts" back as its own menu item, scoped to just facts+summary; chats are
untouched either way, and it goes through cloudMemory/scheduleCloudSave
for signed-in users the same way the rest of memory handling does.

commits.subject: Land on a fresh chat by default on refresh/sign-in; AI-generated chat titles
commits.body:
New Settings section "On Refresh / Sign-In": Start New Chat (default) vs
Resume Last Chat. New-chat mode doesn't actually create an empty chat
record on every load — it just clears activeChatId and shows the
empty-state landing screen; the chat only gets created (via the existing
saveActiveChat -> createChat lazy-create path) once a message is actually
sent. Refactored newChat()'s creation logic out into createChat() so that
lazy path doesn't re-render the DOM mid-send (it used to call newChat()
directly, which wipes #chat-box via renderActiveChat() right as the first
bubble was being appended — a live bug this surfaced). All three landing
paths (tryResumeSession, enterApp, loadCloudChats) now go through one
landOnChat() helper so the setting applies consistently everywhere.

Chat titles: the instant truncated-first-message title is now just a
placeholder — after a chat's first reply, generateChatTitle() quietly asks
the model for a proper 3-6 word title in the background and swaps it in,
same idea as ChatGPT's auto-titling.

commits.subject: Show Live Voice captions one line at a time instead of the whole reply at once
commits.body:
liveTranscript used to get the entire raw (markdown-unstripped) reply
dumped in as one block the instant TTS started. Now strips markdown
formatting and paces it out one sentence at a time, timed proportionally
to the audio's actual duration (falling back to a ~150wpm estimate before
duration is known) — reads like real captions instead of a wall of text.
Timer is cleared on call end, re-entering listening state, and toggling
captions off mid-reply so nothing keeps updating a stale/hidden line.

commits.subject: Fix formatting of choice-hint in index.html
Add Vercel support alongside Netlify, sharing all logic and storage
commits.body:
functions/*.js keeps the Netlify handler format untouched. A new api/
directory (Vercel's function convention) holds one-line wrappers per
route, adapted via functions/_vercelAdapter.js — a shim that translates
Vercel's (req, res) into the (event, context) => {statusCode, headers,
body} shape Netlify handlers already expect. No business logic is
duplicated between the two.

index.html needs zero changes: it always calls /.netlify/functions/*, and
vercel.json rewrites those same paths to /api/* on Vercel, so both
deployments answer identical URLs from one codebase.

Storage needs no migration either — @netlify/blobs here already runs in
"manual mode" (getStore with an explicit siteID + token), which just makes
authenticated HTTPS calls to Netlify's Blobs API regardless of which
platform the calling function runs on. Pointing both deployments at the
same NETLIFY_SITE_ID/NETLIFY_BLOBS_TOKEN keeps WebAuthn creds and cloud
chats in sync across both.

Documented the dual-deploy setup and its one real caveat (WebAuthn is
origin-bound, so the security-key Owner Mode path only works from
whichever single origin RP_ID/ORIGIN are set to) in the README.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: Merge remote-tracking branch 'origin/main'
Give Vercel its own independent storage instead of sharing Netlify Blobs
commits.body:
Netlify and Vercel deployments now keep fully separate data (WebAuthn
credentials, cloud chats) rather than both pointing at the same Netlify
Blobs store. functions/_store.js picks the backend automatically at
runtime via process.env.VERCEL: Netlify keeps using @netlify/blobs
unchanged, Vercel uses a private Vercel Blob store (access: 'private' --
reads require the store's own token, not just a guessable URL, so it's
the same "only this server can read it" guarantee Netlify's manual-mode
siteID+token gives). Every function that touches storage now goes through
this one abstraction instead of calling @netlify/blobs directly.

Verified the Vercel-side get/setJSON logic end-to-end against a mocked
@vercel/blob (missing-key -> null, JSON round-trip through the stream
response) before wiring it into the real functions.

Also disabled Vercel's Deployment Protection (SSO) on the knowura project
via the Vercel MCP, since it was gating the public app behind a
Vercel-account login wall with no custom domain to exempt it, and
provisioned the private Blob store + confirmed BLOB_READ_WRITE_TOKEN
auto-injected into the project's env vars.

Updated the README's dual-deploy section to match: independent storage,
no NETLIFY_SITE_ID/NETLIFY_BLOBS_TOKEN needed on Vercel, and Owner Mode's
security-key path needs registering separately per platform since
credentials no longer sync between them.

lattice with a live timer ('Thinking' / 'Searching the web'). When the
model returned reasoning, the answer starts with a 'Thought for 4.2s'

commits.body:

extractFacts() instead of ask() (identical try/fetch shape), so every
message failed with 'Connection lost' and extractFacts also left the send
button stuck in its busy state. Moved it into ask().

since ask() swallows its own errors into the 'Connection lost' bubble and

timer beside it. The package's React component is a thin wrapper over a
framework-free canvas engine, so the MIT-licensed engine is vendored
under assets/vendor/thinking-orbs and driven by a small vanilla loop
(dynamic import, so a failed load never blocks chat). The finished

search use the same orb (search just changes the label, then switches to

commits.subject: Cut rendering cost: lighter glass, cheaper glow, no fixed wallpaper
commits.body:
- body wallpaper no longer background-attachment: fixed (body never
  scrolls, so it looks identical but avoids the repaint penalty)
- smaller backdrop blur radii on the always-on glass panels (sidebar,
  chat pane, prompt box, cookie notice) and no brightness() in the chain
- BorderGlow: dropped the blend modes (plus-lighter/soft-light) and the
  four widest blurred halo shadows, smaller halo layer
- glow pointer handling measures once on enter and applies at most once
  per animation frame instead of a layout read + style write per event
- cheaper spark glow at Ultra

commits.subject: Big performance and memory pass: Lite mode, smaller images, leak fixes
commits.body:
Root cause of the lag: the wallpaper was a 6000x4000 JPEG (2.8 MB, ~96 MB
decoded) sitting under several backdrop-blurred panels. Now 1920px
(46 KB, ~9 MB decoded) with a 1280px lite variant; the 1080px logo is
320px.

Lite mode (html.lite) removes backdrop blur, the prompt-box glow layers,
sparks, filters and all animations, uses the small wallpaper, and renders
the thinking orbs as a static frame. Settings -> Performance: Auto
(default; Lite when the device reports <=4 GB RAM or <=2 cores, or when a
lag watchdog sees sustained slow frames during interaction), Lite or Full.
Decided in a tiny head script so weak devices never paint the heavy
version first.

Memory: the Live Voice avatar gif loads only during a call and is released
after; music no longer preloads; TTS analyser nodes are disconnected and
the base64 audio dropped when a reply ends; chat DOM capped at 80 nodes,
guest chats at 40, saved reasoning at 6000 chars. marked and
simplewebauthn no longer block page load (defer).

check-init now finds the app script by size (the head has a small one),
and also exercises the performance-mode switch.

commits.subject: Add a Balanced performance tier and soften the chat animation
commits.body:
Full / Balanced / Lite. Balanced keeps the liquid-glass feel without the
costly parts: big panels (sidebar, chat pane) drop backdrop blur and get a
specular edge + soft gradient instead, blur stays only on the small prompt
box and popups, the glow keeps its cursor-following ring but not the halo
layers, and the smaller wallpaper is used. Auto now picks Lite for weak
devices, Balanced for mid ones (<=8 GB and <=4 cores) and Full otherwise,
and the lag watchdog steps down one tier at a time (Full -> Balanced ->
Lite) instead of jumping straight to Lite.

Chat bubbles now fade in over 0.16s with a 4px rise (was 0.3s / 10px) in
every mode.

commits.subject: Ultra Think shows the normal thinking row plus a red bolt; fix tables on mobile
commits.body:
Ultra Think no longer swaps the row for a lone pulsing bolt: it's the
identical animated row (orb, label, live timer, chevron, search stage)
with one red lightning bolt in front, in both the working and finished
states; the red dashed box is gone too.

Tables: markdown tables were width:100% inside a shrink-to-fit bubble, so
on phones they overflowed and got clipped or crushed. New replies wrap
each table in a horizontal scroll container (table sizes to its content,
min column width, wrapped words) and a CSS fallback does the same for
tables already saved in older chats. Bubbles get min-width:0 and tighter
padding/cell padding on small screens.

commits.subject: Auto performance now looks at the GPU, not just RAM
commits.body:
A 16 GB laptop struggling at Full while a phone was fine showed RAM isn't
the bottleneck: blur/glow cost is GPU compositing, and the hover glow only
runs where there's a mouse. Auto now detects the GPU class in the head
script (no WebGL or a software renderer -> Lite; integrated Intel GPU ->
Balanced) alongside memory/cores. The lag watchdog reacts faster (60
frames, or a few >80ms hitches, e.g. from hovering the glow), and the
7-mask edge-fill layer of the prompt glow, the costliest thing to repaint
on every mouse move, is removed in every tier.

commits.subject: Remove the cursor-following prompt glow; replace with a static aura
commits.body:
The BorderGlow port tracked the mouse and, on every move, repainted a
stack of masked/blended pseudo-elements — exactly the kind of per-frame
main-thread work a weak or integrated GPU can't keep up with, and it did
nothing at all on touch devices.

Replaced with a single blurred pseudo-element (.aura-glow) driven by one
CSS keyframe animation: a slow ambient breathe, brightening and speeding
up on focus. No JS, no pointer listeners, no per-frame style writes — the
compositor thread owns it entirely. Same cyan/blue palette. Removed
initBorderGlow, its pointermove/pointerenter handlers, and every
border-glow-card/cursor-angle/edge-proximity/edge-light CSS rule,
including the Balanced/Lite overrides that existed only to tame it.

commits.subject: Install site icons/manifest/share image and a first-visit intro video
commits.body:
Icons: favicons (ico/svg/16/32/48), Apple touch icon, PWA icons (192/512,
plain + maskable), mstile, a 1200x630 OG/Twitter share image, and
site.webmanifest -- copied from the asset pack into the static root and
linked from every HTML entry point (index, 404, terms, privacy) via the
pack's head snippet, each page's og:url/title adjusted to itself. Icon
links get a ?v=2 cache-buster since a plain logo.png favicon was live
before. brand/{k-mark,logo}.svg copied to assets/brand/ as source assets
(not wired into any UI yet). All 21 files verified 200 + correct
Content-Type over a local static server; site.webmanifest parses.

Intro: a first-visit welcome video overlay, ported from the pack's vanilla
JS/CSS reference into index.html's existing script/theme (reuses .btn-ui
for the buttons instead of new button CSS). Muted autoplay + playsinline,
'Turn on sound' unmutes in the click handler, Skip/Esc/ended/error all
close it so it can never trap a visitor, portrait viewports get the tall
video, locks and restores scroll, respects prefers-reduced-motion (marks
seen without autoplaying), ?intro=1 and window.knowuraIntro.replay()/
.reset() for testing. Seen-state is localStorage-only and the DOM is never
built for a returning visitor, so there's no cost for them. Added a
'Replay Intro' item to the settings menu.

Hosting: merged the pack's cache headers into vercel.json (kept the
existing rewrites) and added the Netlify equivalent as per-path [[headers]]
blocks in netlify.toml (Netlify's 'for' pattern doesn't support the regex
alternation Vercel's 'source' does). No CSP or service worker exists yet,
so nothing to adjust there.

Verified end-to-end with Playwright against a real Chromium: fresh visit
shows the overlay muted and picks the right video for a 1280x720 and a
390x844 viewport, sound toggle unmutes, Skip closes it and restores
scroll, a reload does not show it again, ?intro=1 forces a replay, Esc
also closes it -- 15/15 relevant checks passed. The only two console
messages during the run (a Google Identity 403 and a 404 for a Netlify
function) are pre-existing and reproduce identically against the
unmodified code, confirmed by testing the same page before these changes.

check-init.js gained a location/document.body stub (the intro script is
the app's first use of either) and a check that window.knowuraIntro
exposes replay()/reset() without throwing.

Assumptions: the pack was found at public/icons/ instead of the prompt's
./knowura-web-pack/ -- treated as the same pack. Left public/icons/ (the
pack itself) out of this commit and untracked, per 'don't delete until I
say so', to avoid duplicating ~9 MB of video/icon binaries in git history;
delete it whenever you're done referencing it. og:url is set per-page
(home/404/terms/privacy) rather than the pack's single hardcoded
homepage URL, since leaving every page's share preview pointing at the
homepage would be a real bug. The intro overlay is wired into index.html
only (the actual app entry with the login/guest screen) -- not into the
static 404/terms/privacy pages, which aren't the 'first visit' experience
the pack describes. Manually verified icons/video files for corruption
(dimensions, codecs via ffprobe were unavailable locally, but Playwright's
real Chromium loaded and served both mp4s with a 200 and video/mp4
content-type) -- none were missing or corrupt, so no SVG regeneration was
needed.

Manual steps left: redeploy on Vercel (and Netlify if still live), then
hard-refresh / clear cache once to pick up the new favicon over the old
cached logo.png one.

commits.subject: Performance pass: non-blocking fonts, cache headers, Firefox tier fix, new logo
commits.body:
Font loading: the Google Fonts stylesheet was render-blocking on all four
pages. Switched to the media="print" + onload swap pattern (with a
noscript fallback) so first paint no longer waits on it -- verified with
Playwright that Geist Pixel still loads and applies correctly everywhere
afterward.

Cache headers: assets/images, assets/audio, assets/vendor and assets/brand
had no explicit Cache-Control at all (only video/icons got headers when
those were added). Gave them the same public, max-age=86400,
stale-while-revalidate=604800 policy already used for icons -- deliberately
NOT "immutable" with a year-long max-age like video/icons, since these
filenames aren't content-hashed and do get edited in place (e.g. the
wallpaper resize earlier this session); a long immutable cache would risk
serving a stale image/audio file to returning visitors after a redeploy.
Added to both vercel.json and netlify.toml.

Firefox tier fix: user reported real lag on Firefox but not Chrome on the
same machine. Root cause: Firefox's backdrop-filter compositing is well-
documented to be much slower than Chromium's regardless of hardware, and
Auto's tier detection couldn't see it either way -- Firefox doesn't expose
navigator.deviceMemory at all, and masks the WEBGL_debug_renderer_info
string our GPU check relies on, so Auto was defaulting Firefox straight to
Full. Auto now caps Firefox at Balanced (blur/glow reduced) regardless of
what the memory/GPU checks report, in both the <head> decision script and
computePerfTier(). Verified with Playwright: real Firefox now lands on
"balanced", Chromium's detection is unaffected.

Logo: replaced assets/images/logo.png (the old 1080x1080 PNG) with the
icon pack's assets/brand/k-mark.svg everywhere it was used (startup
screen, sidebar, empty-state, and the legal-brand/404 art on all three
legal pages) and deleted the old file. Every usage site only sets one CSS
dimension (height, or width for .notfound img) so the SVG's own aspect
ratio is preserved with no stretching. Verified with Playwright that the
new image actually loads (naturalWidth/Height nonzero) on every page.
